title: While others wait
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you listen to every opinion, or only to the ones with facts behind them?

Jose reminded the group that this call was for people who had made a commitment to study and learn to become better entrepreneurs. It requires commitment, he said, as I am committed to extracting as much meaning as possible from what we read.
He pointed to a statement the author read at the launch of his news channel, near the end of the chapter.
to act upon one's convictions, while others wait to create a positive force in a world where cynics abound.
I think it is the essence of who he is, Jose said. While others wait, that is a key thing. He waited for nobody. Nothing anybody said would deter him from his own convictions.

Part of being an entrepreneur, he said, is listening to people, but not to the ones who offer negativity with no facts behind it, just cynicism. We live in a world where everybody says: oh, no, you can't do this.

Time and time again he says: why not? Jose called that possibility thinking. Impossibility thinking is: oh, no, I can't do this, that's not possible. You shut all the doors down before you explore logically whether it can be done.

He addresses everybody in the statement, Jose said: the American people, the cable industry, his employees. His leadership is inclusive. A student said it is like calling his baseball team the people's team: it makes it everybody's.
Jose said he has the ability to include people in his mission. It is a great leadership trait. His ability to build a team is part of his success.
Whose doubts are facts, and whose are just cynicism?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one doubt you hear about your plan.
Write whether it has facts behind it, or is just cynicism.
Rewrite it as a possibility question: why not?
Write who you include in your mission, and how.
Write one door you shut before you explored it.

check.q: What did Jose call 'why not?' thinking?
What kind of negativity did Jose say not to listen to?
choices: The kind with no facts behind it, just cynicism

check.q: What did Jose say about the author's statement and the people he addressed?

recap: Listen to facts, not cynicism. Ask why not.
